units.title: Canonical resolution-to-link quotient
claims: The canonical restriction W->V is a surjection of local systems and has the asserted stalkwise interpretation.
units.checker_scope: A29 does not check the IC truncation or analytic decomposition argument.
units.attribution: Reproduction of the October 7 prop:curve-places input, using Saito's analytic theorem.

units.title: Scheme fibers, countable Quot spaces, and finite invariant lifts
claims: The entire projective analytic scheme family over T algebraizes via an explicit proper ambient embedding.
Fiber line bundles span W rationally, including nonreduced scheme fibers.
Countably many finite-type parameter spaces and finite multisections imply finite monodromy.
Poincare duality and finite-group averaging give b independent invariant lifts through W->V.
units.checker_scope: Only finite permutation and S3 examples are computed; algebraization and finite monodromy of geometric W are prose.
units.attribution: The September 24 projective manuscript Section 6.1 already contains the finite-monodromy parameter argument.

units.title: Loop-carrying compact, Stein neighborhoods, and small factorialization
claims: Invariant fiber classes lift integrally near a full loop-preserving Runge compact.
The lifts have actual Cartier divisor representatives on g inverse of a Stein neighborhood.
Fujino's theorem gives a small projective crepant terminal model over the full compact Kprime.
The finite prescribed Weil divisors have one common Cartier multiple before restriction to a smaller core.
units.checker_scope: No computation checks Stein geometry, coherent vanishing, or factorialization.
units.attribution: Proposed analytic proof of an existing manuscript proposition; full-compact restriction safeguards are part of the old draft, not new results of this review.

units.title: Degrees on all normalized surface-family sheets
claims: The degree map Q^b->Q^s is injective, accounting for every fiber curve, normalization-cover sheet, and nilpotent thickening.
units.checker_scope: The example's degree matrix [1] is checked; the general map's injectivity is not.
units.attribution: Geometric step in the reproduction of the October 7 bound.

units.title: All discrepancy-two places and distinct global primes
claims: Every log-discrepancy-two place centered on the singular curve is already on the specified principalizing resolution.
Restriction to a pi1-surjective curve core is a bijection of all local and global discrepancy-two places.
Distinct surface centers on the small model give distinct global primes.

proof.locator: Theorem B; Section 4, equations (8)-(9) and the cover argument

units.checker_scope: Finite sign and orbit controls do not establish geometric representation or globalization.
units.attribution: Proposed strengthening from an injection to a bijection; novelty not checked or asserted.

units.title: The compact Kahler curve bound
claims: For Y compact Kahler under the exact fixed-resolution hypotheses, b<=N_T for distinct global primes, by b<=s<=N_T.
units.checker_scope: Neither A04 nor A29 is a machine proof of this theorem.
units.attribution: Reproduction of October 7 prop:curve-places, not a new termination theorem.

units.title: Proposed removal of the ambient Kahler hypothesis
claims: The curve bound and globalization bijection hold for compact complex Y without Kahlerness, retaining global projectivity of the specified resolution and every other hypothesis.

proof.locator: Theorem A scope extension; Section 4 final paragraph

units.checker_scope: No test compares Kahler and non-Kahler geometry.
units.attribution: Proposed strengthening, not an independently established novelty claim.

units.title: Conditional branch and junction consequence
claims: Summing the curve bounds over distinct centers gives sum b_T<=tau_Y(Q).
With the separate Section 05 topological inequality one obtains the branch inequality.
The junction and termination consequences additionally require separate Section 07 weights and other programs.
units.checker_scope: No branch topology, local weight, descent, or termination theorem is computed.
units.attribution: Conditional downstream implication only; no review of unrelated antecedents.

units.title: Global quadric-cone product realizing b=N_T=1
claims: The projective quadric cone times P1 is a terminal fourfold with the specified principalizing resolution.
Its unique global exceptional prime has relative canonical coefficient 1 and log discrepancy 2.
The O(-1,-1) circle-bundle link gives constant V of rank 1 and hence b=N_T=1.
The small-resolution degree matrix is [1].
units.checker_scope: Polynomial charts, selected identities and ranks only; not the topological or bundle identifications.
units.attribution: Classical ordinary-double-point construction used as a sharpness example; originality not asserted.

units.title: Terminal codimension-two smoothness and discrepancy conventions
claims: The transverse-surface argument in Appendix A supplies terminal-fourfold smoothness in codimension two.
A terminal normal surface has no exceptional curves on its minimal resolution.
A smooth codimension-c blowup has log discrepancy c.
Composition adds positive relative canonical coefficients, not their negatives and not the log discrepancies themselves.
units.checker_scope: The bounded rational sweep checks a sign pattern, not analytic surface theory or slicing.
units.attribution: Standard local singularity facts with a prose reconstruction; original Grauert source was not retrieved in the old work.

units.title: Retired simply connected disc shortcut
claims: One cannot infer a count of distinct global primes by counting branches after dropping the curve loops: a transitive two-sheet cover can split.
units.checker_scope: Explicit finite permutation negative control only, not a realized fourfold counterexample.
units.attribution: Failed Argus proof shortcut, not a refutation of an original manuscript.

units.title: Retired averaging without finite monodromy
claims: A surjective equivariant quotient need not surject on invariant sections for infinite monodromy; the displayed unipotent quotient is a counterexample to that linear-algebra shortcut.
units.checker_scope: An exact two-dimensional representation, not a geometric counterexample to the curve bound.
units.attribution: Failed Argus proof shortcut; CP_MONODROMY is the proposed geometric repair.
